questions.q: Two independent events $A$ and $B$ have $P(A) = \frac{3}{4}$ and $P(B) = \frac{9}{10}$. Find $P(A \mathrm{\ and\ } B)$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $\frac{27}{40}$. Independent events multiply: $P(A)\times P(B) = \frac{3}{4}\times\frac{9}{10} = \frac{27}{40}$.

questions.q: Two independent events $A$ and $B$ have $P(A) = \frac{1}{5}$ and $P(B) = \frac{3}{10}$. Find $P(A \mathrm{\ and\ } B)$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $\frac{3}{50}$. Independent events multiply: $P(A)\times P(B) = \frac{1}{5}\times\frac{3}{10} = \frac{3}{50}$.

questions.q: A student scored $82, 88, 91,$ and $85$ on four exams. What score must the student earn on the fifth exam to achieve an overall mean score of $88$?
questions.answer: Required total for 5 exams: $5 \times 88 = 440$. Current sum: $82 + 88 + 91 + 85 = 346$. Fifth score required: $440 - 346 = 94$.
questions.explanation: Required total for 5 exams: $5 \times 88 = 440$. Current sum: $82 + 88 + 91 + 85 = 346$. Fifth score required: $440 - 346 = 94$.

questions.q: In a set of 7 integers: $\{4, 7, 9, x, 14, 18, 20\}$ arranged in ascending order, the median is equal to the mean. What is the value of $x$?
questions.answer: Median of 7 sorted values is the 4th value: $x$. Mean $= \frac{4 + 7 + 9 + x + 14 + 18 + 20}{7} = \frac{72 + x}{7}$. Equating: $7x = 72 + x \Rightarrow 6x = 72 \Rightarrow x = 12$.
questions.explanation: Median of 7 sorted values is the 4th value: $x$. Mean $= \frac{4 + 7 + 9 + x + 14 + 18 + 20}{7} = \frac{72 + x}{7}$. Equating: $7x = 72 + x \Rightarrow 6x = 72 \Rightarrow x = 12$.

questions.q: In a chemistry course, homework counts for $20\%$, labs count for $30\%$, and tests count for $50\%$. If a student earns $90$ on homework, $80$ on labs, and $86$ on tests, what is the weighted final grade?
A data set consists of the numbers $\{3, 7, 8, 12, 15, 18, 21\}$. What is the interquartile range (IQR) of this data set?
questions.answer: The median is $12$. The lower half is $\{3, 7, 8\}$ with $Q_1 = 7$. The upper half is $\{15, 18, 21\}$ with $Q_3 = 18$. Thus $\mathrm{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 18 - 7 = 11$.
questions.explanation: The median is $12$. The lower half is $\{3, 7, 8\}$ with $Q_1 = 7$. The upper half is $\{15, 18, 21\}$ with $Q_3 = 18$. Thus $\mathrm{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 18 - 7 = 11$.

questions.q: If every value in a data set is multiplied by $3$ and then increased by $5$, how is the standard deviation $\sigma$ affected?
choices: It is multiplied by $3$ and increased by $5$
questions.answer: Multiplying by a constant $c$ scales standard deviation by $|c| = 3$. Adding a constant shifts the center but does not change the spread. Hence, standard deviation is multiplied by $3$.
questions.explanation: Multiplying by a constant $c$ scales standard deviation by $|c| = 3$. Adding a constant shifts the center but does not change the spread. Hence, standard deviation is multiplied by $3$.

questions.q: Which of the following data sets has a standard deviation equal to $0$?
questions.answer: A standard deviation of $0$ occurs if and only if all values in the data set are identical.
questions.explanation: A standard deviation of $0$ occurs if and only if all values in the data set are identical.

questions.q: A bag contains $6$ red marbles, $8$ blue marbles, and $10$ green marbles. If one marble is selected at random, what is the probability that it is NOT blue?
Two fair standard six-sided dice are rolled simultaneously. What is the probability that the sum of the two numbers rolled is greater than $9$?
questions.answer: Outcomes with sum $> 9$ are sums of $10, 11, 12$: $(4,6), (5,5), (6,4), (5,6), (6,5), (6,6)$ = 6 outcomes. Probability $= \frac{6}{36} = \frac{1}{6}$.
questions.explanation: Outcomes with sum $> 9$ are sums of $10, 11, 12$: $(4,6), (5,5), (6,4), (5,6), (6,5), (6,6)$ = 6 outcomes. Probability $= \frac{6}{36} = \frac{1}{6}$.

sections.heading: Part V — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Exam Application (29–37)

questions.q: Events $A$ and $B$ are independent. If $P(A) = 0.4$ and $P(B) = 0.5$, what is the probability that at least one of the events occurs, $P(A \cup B)$?
questions.answer: For independent events, $P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B) = 0.4 \times 0.5 = 0.2$. Then $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) = 0.4 + 0.5 - 0.2 = 0.70$.
questions.explanation: For independent events, $P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B) = 0.4 \times 0.5 = 0.2$. Then $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) = 0.4 + 0.5 - 0.2 = 0.70$.

questions.q: In how many distinct ways can a committee of $4$ members be chosen from a group of $9$ people?
How many different $4$-digit identification codes can be formed using digits $0$ through $9$ if repetition of digits is not allowed and the first digit cannot be $0$?
questions.answer: Choices for 1st digit (1-9) $= 9$. Choices for 2nd digit (0-9 excluding 1st) $= 9$. Choices for 3rd digit $= 8$. Choices for 4th digit $= 7$. Total $= 9 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7 = 4,536$.
questions.explanation: Choices for 1st digit (1-9) $= 9$. Choices for 2nd digit (0-9 excluding 1st) $= 9$. Choices for 3rd digit $= 8$. Choices for 4th digit $= 7$. Total $= 9 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7 = 4,536$.

questions.q: A restaurant offers $4$ appetizers, $6$ main courses, and $3$ desserts. How many distinct 3-course dinner combinations are possible?
questions.answer: By the fundamental counting principle: $4 \times 6 \times 3 = 72$ combinations.
questions.explanation: By the fundamental counting principle: $4 \times 6 \times 3 = 72$ combinations.

questions.q: A data set of 9 values has a mean of 54. A new value of 224 is added. What is the new mean?
